content: {"summary":"Inventory-service pods see intermittent DNS failures while datastore VMs are fine; this points to the two internal DNS servers having different zone data after a rollout. You can demonstrate the disagreement by querying each DNS server directly (dig) and comparing the SOA serials or answers.","likely_cause":"Inconsistent zone files between internal-dns-01 and internal-dns-02, where one server missed the `inventory-db-01.prod.internal` record after the March 2026 rollout.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Intermittent pod DNS failures while VMs are fine indicate DNS server disagreement","evidence_ids":["RB-020#6"],"quote":"Pods failing intermittently while VMs are fine is the fingerprint of the two servers disagreeing."},{"text":"The March 2026 rollout left one DNS server missing the inventory-db record","evidence_ids":["RB-020#13"],"quote":"the new file was missing `inventory-db-01.prod.internal`"},{"text":"Run dig against each DNS server and compare SOA serials to show disagreement","evidence_ids":["RB-020#7"],"quote":"Read the `status:` in each header and compare the SOA serials."},{"text":"CoreDNS forward plugin picks upstream at random, so pods see cached answers from whichever server responded last","evidence_ids":["RB-020#3"],"quote":"If the two servers disagree, pods see whichever answer was cached last"}],"next_checks":["Run dig @10.0.0.53 and @10.0.0.54 for inventory-db-01.prod.internal and note any NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL responses","Compare the prod.internal SOA serial numbers from both servers","SSH into each internal-dns VM and grep the zone file for the inventory-db record","Check CoreDNS logs on the server that returned NXDOMAIN for recent errors","Clear CoreDNS cache on pods or restart the CoreDNS deployment to verify the fix after correcting the zone"]}
